summary: Practise JIAF 2 analysis, needs prioritisation and resource allocation. Strengthen assessment decisions with this five-day course.
lede: Humanitarian needs assessment helps response practitioners turn field evidence into clear priorities when data is incomplete. Designed for assessment, information-management and response-planning practitioners, the course covers secondary-data review, evidence-quality checks, triangulation, severity analysis and community validation. Participants compare needs with response capacity, set prioritisation criteria and document cost-aware allocation trade-offs while recording uncertainty.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is for practitioners who collect, analyse, validate or use humanitarian needs evidence to shape response priorities and resource decisions.
audience: Sector or Cluster Information Management Officers
Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning Officers
prerequisites: Designed for practitioners with working experience in humanitarian assessment, information management or response planning. Programming is not required; exercises use Excel and assessment-analysis methods.
